heading: INT. FORMER BOWLING ALLEY - EVIDENCE ANNEX - NIGHT

units.text: INT. FORMER BOWLING ALLEY - EVIDENCE ANNEX - NIGHT
Lane 12 is a ghost of itself.
Waxed maple, gutters stacked with cardboard banker's boxes.
Overhead, a dead scoreboard still reads HOME 114 / GUEST 98.
DET. ADAEZE OKONKWO, 40s, rain-wet trench coat, reading glasses pushed up into close-cropped hair, walks the lane like she owns the lease.
At the ball return sits SGT. HALVARD PEDERSEN, 60, heavy, a thermos between his knees, pretending not to be asleep.
Who signed the boxes out?
units.name: OKONKWO

units.text: Nobody. That's the problem.
units.name: PEDERSEN

units.text: A TECH in a paper suit kneels at the far end, photographing a box lid with a ring light.
Young, narrow shoulders, earbuds in one ear only.
You. What's your name?
units.name: OKONKWO

units.text: Just Tech tonight. Ask the lab.
units.name: TECH

units.text: She moves on.
Doesn't push.
By the shoe-rental counter, MRS. KOWALCZYK, 70s, cardigan buttoned wrong, clutches a handbag like a flotation device.
She owned this alley for thirty years.
Strike night was Thursdays. Forty-one lanes of noise. Now listen to it.
units.name: MRS. KOWALCZYK

units.text: Silence.
A compressor hums somewhere.
Ma'am, did you give anyone a key?
units.name: OKONKWO

units.text: The city has my keys. The city has everything.
units.name: MRS. KOWALCZYK

units.text: Ain't that the truth.
units.name: PEDERSEN

units.text: OFFICER TRAN, 20s, stiff, enters from the lobby with a clipboard.
He stops at the edge of the lane, unsure if he's allowed to step on it.
Detective. Gate log's clean. Last entry, six forty p.m. Someone named Lennox.
units.name: OFFICER TRAN

units.text: First name?
units.name: OKONKWO

units.text: Just Lennox.
units.name: OFFICER TRAN

units.text: Behind a stack of boxes, a cough.
Everyone looks.
LENNOX, 50s, gray ponytail, security lanyard, stands up slowly from where he's been sitting on a crate, hands visible and empty.
I'm the night man. I was in the office.
units.name: LENNOX

units.text: Mr. Lennox. You've been in the building the whole time.
units.name: OKONKWO

units.text: It's a warm building.
units.name: LENNOX

units.text: The Tech glances up, finally pulls the earbud out.
Bashir. It's Bashir. Since you asked.
units.name: TECH

units.text: Thank you, Bashir.
units.name: OKONKWO

units.text: Box nineteen has been opened. Seal's cut clean. Razor, not a knife.
units.name: BASHIR

units.text: How do you know?
units.name: OKONKWO

units.text: Edge doesn't tear. I do this for a living.
units.name: BASHIR

units.text: Okonkwo takes off her glasses.
Folds them.
Looks at Lennox for a long, unhurried moment.
Walk me through the office, Mr. Lennox.
units.name: OKONKWO

units.text: Sure.
units.name: LENNOX

units.text: He doesn't move.
Neither does she.
I'll get the coffee.
units.name: PEDERSEN

units.text: He doesn't move either.
Light's good here, if anyone wants to take their time.
units.name: BASHIR

units.text: Okonkwo sits down on the foul line, crosses her legs, and waits.
